1. The HydroSense project service
HydroSense accompanies the water filtration thesis project. Depending on compatible hardware, connectivity, permissions, and enabled features, it may display pH, total dissolved solids (TDS), turbidity, tank level or distance, leak or moisture status, pump status and runtime, and filter-life estimates. Authorized users may send commands to supported equipment.

The service depends on correctly configured hardware, a working network, Firebase authentication and database services, and ongoing project resources. Features and support may change as the thesis project develops. Where reasonably possible, Group 1 will explain significant planned service changes or shutdowns in advance. Urgent safety or security action may require immediate interruption.

HydroSense supports monitoring and operation; it is not an emergency, medical, flood, fire, life-safety, or certified water-treatment safety system. Keep appropriate independent safeguards, local shutoffs, and supervision for the physical installation. Inspect and maintain pumps, valves, sensors, wiring, power supplies, tanks, filters, and safety devices in accordance with suitable instructions and qualified advice.

Commands and displayed states may be delayed, duplicated, rejected, unavailable, or inaccurate because of network, cloud-service, power, sensor, firmware, or hardware problems. A displayed pump state does not establish that a relay or pump is physically operating. Hardware safety overrides may stop equipment despite an app command. These limitations do not excuse a party from duties imposed by law.

4. Monitoring and water-quality information
Readings and range labels describe only the measurements available from the configured sensors. A reading within a configured range does not establish that water is safe to drink. The app does not test every contaminant, provide laboratory analysis or certification, or replace qualified health, engineering, plumbing, or water-treatment advice.

Do not decide whether to drink, distribute, or otherwise use water from in-app readings alone. Use appropriate testing and qualified advice for decisions involving health, safety, building requirements, or regulatory compliance.

5. Filter-life estimates
Filter-health and remaining-life information is an estimate based on sensor readings, runtime, configured assumptions, and, where applicable, simulated or nominal telemetry. Follow inspection, cleaning, replacement, and manufacturer instructions. An estimate does not establish that filter media remain effective or that the filtered water is potable.

HYDROSENSE PRIVACY POLICY

Project operator and personal information controller: Group 1
Contact: ciriloenriquez123@gmail.com
Effective date: October 15, 2026
Revision: 2026-10-15.2

Group 1 is the student thesis team responsible for the water filtration system and HydroSense, its companion monitoring and control software. The team operates the project service and determines the purposes and means of project-managed personal information processing. Contact the team at the address above about that responsibility, your data, or the people handling a request. Sign-in and infrastructure providers may also have responsibilities for processing they determine independently.

This Policy describes information used to operate the companion app. Acknowledging it is not blanket consent to unrelated data use or participation in a thesis study. Any separate collection of personal information for research needs a specific notice and an appropriate lawful basis, including separate consent where required.

1. Information we may handle
Account information: When you register or sign in, HydroSense may handle your email address, display name, Firebase user identifier, authentication provider, and profile information made available by Google or Facebook when you choose those sign-in methods.

Water-system information: HydroSense may receive and display data sent by your connected system, including pH, TDS, turbidity, tank level, tank distance, tank warnings, leak or moisture status, pump statuses, control-mode information, pump runtime counters, and other supported sensor or hardware values.

Filter and app information: The app may store filter-health estimates, filter service actions, model observations, consent status, selected language, theme preference, saved-account display information, and other settings needed to provide the requested features. Some of this information is stored locally on your device.

Technical and security information: Firebase and other service providers may process technical information needed to authenticate users, maintain connections, protect the service, prevent abuse, diagnose failures, and deliver their services.

2. How information is collected
Information may come from you during registration or account use, from Google or Facebook when you select their sign-in options, from Firebase Authentication, from your connected ESP32 or other supported hardware, and from your device while the app is running.

3. How we use information
Group 1 may use information to create and secure accounts; authenticate users; display live monitoring data; send and reflect authorized control commands; provide tank, leak, pump, and filter features; calculate filter-health estimates; remember settings and saved accounts; respond to support or deletion requests; maintain, secure, troubleshoot, and improve HydroSense; and comply with legal obligations.

4. Services and sharing
HydroSense relies on Firebase Authentication and Realtime Database services to support accounts and synchronized monitoring or control data. If you choose Google or Facebook sign-in, the selected provider processes information under its own terms and privacy policy. Group 1 may share information with service providers needed to operate HydroSense or where a lawful obligation or other applicable legal basis permits it. Project information is not automatically available for unrelated research or a transfer to another operator; any such change requires an appropriate notice and lawful basis. Group 1 does not sell your personal information.

5. Connected-system access
System readings and control data may be shared among authorized operators and hardware in the thesis installation. Signing in does not necessarily create a private system or separate copy of its data. Access depends on the permissions configured for the connected service. Only connect or operate equipment you are authorized to use. Group 1 remains responsible for access controls and other safeguards required of it by law.

6. Storage and retention
Account and system data may remain in Firebase while your account or the connected service is active, or for as long as reasonably needed for security, legal, backup, dispute, and operational purposes. Consent records, settings, saved-account metadata, and filter history may remain on your device until you clear them, remove the app, use an available reset feature, or request assistance. Deleting the app does not by itself delete Firebase account or system data.

7. Security
Group 1 uses reasonable measures available within the app and its configured services to protect information. No internet transmission, authentication system, database, device, or physical installation is completely secure. You are responsible for protecting your credentials, devices, network, and connected equipment.

8. Your choices and requests
You may stop using a sign-in provider, update information supported by the app, remove saved-account information from the device, or contact Group 1 at ciriloenriquez123@gmail.com to ask about access, correction, deletion, or other privacy concerns. We may need to verify your identity before completing a request. You may withdraw consent for processing that relies on consent. Processing needed to deliver a requested service, comply with law, or meet another valid legal basis is not treated as optional consent merely because you accepted the Terms. Removing necessary account data may prevent related features from working. If information must be retained under an applicable obligation or other valid basis, Group 1 will explain the relevant reason when responding to your request. You may also raise a complaint with the Philippine National Privacy Commission; contacting Group 1 first is not a condition imposed by this Policy.

9. Adults only
HydroSense is intended for people who are at least 18 years old. We do not knowingly invite children under 18 to create accounts. If you believe a person under 18 provided information, contact Group 1 so the matter can be reviewed.

10. Changes to this Policy
Each edition states its effective date and revision. When an app update changes the bundled Terms or this Policy, HydroSense presents a change summary and the full documents and requires renewed acceptance of the Terms and acknowledgement of the Policy before continued use of the project service. Updated documents remain available in About HydroSense. Changes apply prospectively and do not remove existing rights. Acknowledgement alone does not authorize a new processing purpose that requires separate consent or another lawful basis.

11. Contact
For privacy questions, data requests, or concerns about HydroSense, contact Group 1 at ciriloenriquez123@gmail.com. This Policy is governed by applicable laws of the Philippines, subject to any mandatory rights that apply to you.

A least-squares model learns how fast each stage wears from TDS, turbidity and pH, applied to the measured five-stage pump run time. Pump A is intake-only and never counts toward filter wear. The model starts from simulated wear data and begins learning from your recorded services once enough have accumulated.
